raw_response:
I farm a big area, so I will not play around too much. I will do mostly what has worked before, because missing yield on this much land hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. Around here, if cotton looks weak in the early stage, it is hard to pull it back later, so I will feed it a little heavier and keep water ready from the well. I watch what other good growers around Quzhou do, and nobody on land like this size can manage by hand like a tiny household plot. I will keep the main land in cotton because that is my money crop, and I will keep a smaller piece in maize so I have a steadier harvest and do not put everything in one basket. For cotton, I will use improved seed, plough the land, put enough base fertilizer, irrigate a few times when the field really needs it, and spray more often because cotton always attracts more trouble. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, fertilize well at planting and topdress once, water fewer times than cotton, and spray less. I do not like cutting fertilizer too much. On a big farm, losing even 30 or 40 kilos per mu across many mu is a big loss.
